name: Jahaziel
overview: Jahaziel was a male figure noted in the Bible primarily as the father of Shecaniah, who accompanied Ezra during the return from exile. While his tribal affiliation is not specified, his role as a father to a significant participant in Ezra's journey highlights his place in the post-exilic community. There are no additional notes recorded about him.
namesAndTitles: The name Jahaziel means 'G-d [El] will see,' reflecting a theologically rich meaning common in Hebrew names. This name is a proper name mentioned in Ezra 8:5, though it was not given directly by God.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture identifies Jahaziel as a descendant of Zattu, and he is the father of Shecaniah, who was among those who returned with Ezra. Beyond this, no further familial details are recorded in the biblical text.
scriptureSignificance: Jahaziel's significance lies in his connection to the post-exilic restoration under Ezra, as his son Shecaniah was part of the group that returned to Jerusalem. This association places Jahaziel within the context of God's providential care for His people during their return and rebuilding efforts. Though Jahaziel himself is not described in detail, his familial link to a key returnee underscores the continuity of God's covenant community.
